purpose: Reviewed allowlist of every line by which the composed production Firestore Rules differ from what production main deploys. 2.5.0 (main 36b648ad) deploys the same Rules as 2.4.0; the hunks below are R93-07 (LOCK MY SIGNINGS expression budget). Regenerate only with node tests/support/composed-production-rules.cjs --print-main-delta origin/main, then review every hunk.

added: // R93-07 (hunt T2-1): three rows picked from the name list (overall + position + playerId each) took LOCK MY SIGNINGS past the
// 1,000-expression limit. Same checks, cheaper form: an absent optional key reads as an in-range default (one lookup, one let),
// a key that is present still has to be an int in range (overall 30..99, playerId 1..999999) or one of the 15 positions;
// null, a float, a string or an unknown position is refused as before. The position list is one anchored regex (a list
// literal costs one expression per item); the catalog regexes alone check the ids (they are a subset of the option ids).
hunks.why: R93-07 comment: why the signing row validator is written in its cheaper form (hunt T2-1, three picked signings refused by the 1,000-expression limit).

added: // r91 (2.4.0): the SoFIFA id of a player picked from the Transfer War autocomplete (optional; a typed name has none).
hunks.why: R93-07: the optional overall, playerId and position keys are read once each with an in-range default; a present key is still checked exactly as before.

removed: && (!('overall' in value) || (value.overall is int && value.overall >= 30 && value.overall <= 99))
// r91 (2.4.0): the SoFIFA id of a player picked from the Transfer War autocomplete (optional; a typed name has none).
&& (!('playerId' in value) || (value.playerId is int && value.playerId >= 1 && value.playerId <= 999999))
hunks.why: R93-07: the same three optional-key checks on the let values (int ranges unchanged; the 15 positions as one anchored regex instead of a 15-item list literal).
R93-07: the option-id regex in front of the league catalog regex is dropped; the league catalog is a subset of the option ids, so the result is identical.
R93-07: the option-id regex in front of the nationality catalog regex is dropped; the nationality catalog is a subset of the option ids, so the result is identical.

added: // R93-07: one diff instead of an exact key list plus seven equalities. The stored document was created with exact keys
// (ssjrTransferPrivateBase), so a lock may change or add only these keys; schemaVersion, objectType, rivalryId,
// seasonNumber, managerRole, guesses and guessLockedAt stay exactly as stored. guessSalt may only appear as null on an
// r66 document (the equality below), and the salt keys stay both-or-neither.
hunks.why: R93-07 comment: why the private signing lock checks the stored role document with one diff.
R93-07: one affectedKeys().hasOnly diff replaces the exact key list and five identity equalities (the document was created with exact keys); the salt both-or-neither rule stays.
R93-07: guesses and guessLockedAt are outside the allowed diff keys, so they still cannot change at the signing lock.
